core_obligations: Settle the bounded below case: the comparison map from the alternating Cech complex to the usual Cech complex is a quasi-isomorphism by the cited lemma, since the map of double complexes is an isomorphism on the first pages of the second spectral sequences and these converge (proof lines 10232-10246).
Conclude the bounded below case by combining that quasi-isomorphism with the cited comparison of the usual Cech complex with derived global sections and assumption (3)(a) (proof lines 10247-10248).

For the general case, use assumption (3)(c) to choose a K-injective resolution F^bullet -> I^bullet = lim I_n^bullet and rewrite the comparison map as the derived-category arrow lim_n Tot(Cech_alt(U, tau_{>= -n}F^bullet)) -> Gamma(X, I^bullet) = lim_n Gamma(X, I_n^bullet) (proof lines 10251-10264).
Check that each tau_{>= -n}F^bullet is a bounded below complex satisfying the hypotheses, so the bounded below case makes each comparison map a quasi-isomorphism (proof lines 10265-10274).

Use finiteness of the alternating Cech complex to see that the cohomology on the left is eventually constant, deduce the same on the right, and identify the cohomology of the limit with that constant value by the Mittag-Leffler lemma (proof lines 10274-10283).
proof_roadmap: Prove the bounded below case through the second spectral sequence of the double complex and convergence.
Choose a K-injective resolution and express the map as a limit over truncations.
Apply the bounded below case to each truncation and use eventual constancy plus Mittag-Leffler to pass to the limit.
difficulty_reason: The lemma extends the comparison map from the alternating Cech complex of a finite open covering to RGamma(X, F^bullet) from bounded below complexes to arbitrary complexes of O_X-modules, assuming the obvious sheaf-vanishing conditions on a basis of opens. The bounded-below case is reduced to a second-spectral-sequence comparison together with convergence (proof lines 10232-10248). The general case is genuinely research-level: one chooses a K-injective resolution F^bullet -> I^bullet = lim I_n^bullet using assumption (3)(c), rewrites the comparison map as a limit of maps on the truncations tau_{>= -n}F^bullet, uses that the alternating Cech complex is finite so its cohomology is eventually constant, and then applies a Mittag-Leffler lemma to read off the cohomology of the limit (proof lines 10251-10283). The unbounded limit argument, not the bounded case, is the substance.
